recipes.name: Asian Beef with Snow Peas
ingredients_raw: 1 pound beef round steak, cut into thin strips

steps.text: Combine soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar, and cornstarch in a small bowl until smooth; set aside.

Heat oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Stir-fry ginger and garlic until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add steak and stir-fry until evenly browned, about 2 minutes. Stir in snow peas and cook until crisp-tender, about 3 minutes. Pour in soy sauce mixture and bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until sauce is thickened and smooth. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Asian Beef with Snow Peas
raw_recipe.description: Stir-fried beef with snow peas in a light gingery sauce.

video.description: For a fast weeknight dinner that’s hearty and full of flavor, you’ll love this awesome stir-fry dish. Simply make a sauce of soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar and cornstarch. Get your wok hot, then stir-fry fresh ginger and garlic. Add a pound of beef round steak that you’ve cut into strips, and when browned, add snow peas and sauce, stirring until thick and rich. Serve over rice and enjoy!

review.reviewBody: HELPFUL TIPS AFTER MAKING THIS ALL MY LIFE: Being Asian, I love running into recipes that remind me of things I already make. The most important thing to take from these reviews is to DOUBLE THE SAUCE. My relatives would not want to eat any of these that have made this as is. ...just doesn't taste like anything you'd have at a good restaurant (as this is american chinese, not authentic). Doubling the sauce ingred. was just the right amount of sauce to accompany a side of rice. Don't overcook the steak. Frying until you get a nice brown color is the perfect way to tell if it's done & the estimate times on the recipe are pretty accurate assuming your slices are thin. Any mixture of veggies work (mushrooms, carrots, frozen peas, red peppers, sliced zucchini, water chestnuts) ...or just grabbing a frozen stir-fry bag of veggies. I add half a bag, and use the other half for the crispy orange chicken from this site that I also make when I'm making oriental food for guests. Red Wine VINEGAR is an acceptable substitution, but I'd encourage you to try more recipes on this site using rice vinegar!

I made this recipe twice. I found that the secret is slicing the meat very thin. The suggestion of marinating the meat also added more flavor. I used sugar snap peas the second time instead of snow peas and thought it also added more flavor.

Fantastic! I did marinate the steak, while I was prepping, in an egg white, salt, pepper, corn starch and vegetable oil as I had seen videos of Chinese restaurant chefs doing this. It gave the meat a fantastic coating when it grilled up. I used Mirin (sweetened saki) for the rice wine. I added 2tbs oyster sauce and a splash of sesame oil to the wok just before adding the sauce mixture which I had doubled. Delicious. Sweet. My family loved it and everyone came back for seconds.

One of my favorite recipes and I've tried SOOO many of them! I agree to double the sauce, I added extra water and let it cook down a bit which gave it a nice gravy to go over rice. Word of caution, I used powdered ginger and it is much stronger! I would say to use about half of what it asks for if you are doing that. Oh and I didn't add any bell peppers but did add mushrooms and water chestnuts for the crunch. Yum!!

Tasty sauce but it did need to be doubled. Photo looks nice, BUT if photographing with bell peppers, zucchini & mushrooms they should be listed in ingredients & should have descriptions of when to add etc. Not everyone knows instinctively.

Browned the round steak then added some onion and minced garlic. I doubled the sauce and combined half of it with the meat and spices in a crock pot. Cooked about four hours on medium heat and added the snow peas, carrots, and green pepper along with a little more sliced onion about 15 minutes before plating time. Just before serving I added the sauce with a little extra corn starch to thicken. The sauce and seasoning is everything. It was very tasty, and I will fix again. I'm just not certain it was the absolutely best I have ever had; hence the four star rating.

I added pepper some zucchini, and mushrooms. You should have the steaks frozen so you can slice it really really thin and it turned out beautifully with a round steak. I did double the sauce as everyone suggested added a lot more ginger. It was excellent. I didn't have rice wine so I had to make do with dry vermouth which worked out just fine in rice wine vinegar.

This dish was excellent. I used filet mignon and marinated it in the sherry/soy/brown sugar mixture for about an hour and then discarded it, so the meat was super tender. I made another batch of the sherry/soy/brown sugar with the cornstarch for the thickening part of the recipe. I doubled the sauce. I also added an onion for another veggie in the mix. Snow peas should be barely cooked as they will continue to cook in the sauce when the meat is added back in. Be careful or the snow peas will turn into limp noodles! You could also use broccoli, asparagus, carrots, etc. This was the best recipe I've made from AR in a really long time. It's a keeper and I'll be making this on high rotation!! Thank you!!

Fabulous base recipe! Mirin is a must, cut back on the brown sugar, added some grated garlic & ginger to the sauce using about 1/3-1/2 as a marinade for the meat (flank steak) for about an hour...the meat literally melted in our mouths. I prefer peanut oil for high temps on a wok....used an array of veggies cooked in order of density. Great staple sauce for our stir fry adventures, thanks!

So the flavor of the above recipe is good. I swapped out the rice wine for mirin because that's what I had on hand and it worked out just fine.

My issue was with the sauce, specifically that there wasn't enough of it. On round two I'm going to add in some beef broth and up the corn starch, mirin, and brown sugar a little bit then reduce it down some. That way there is enough sauce to coat my rice, which I'm a big fan of. If you like light sauce though, follow the recipe as is and you won't go wrong.

I made Pork and snow pea instead. I had to make it gluten free. So I tried it with rice wine vinegar - I wasn't sure if rice wine was gluten free - it came out too vinegary so I would lighten up on the rice wine vinegar. Instead of cornstarch I used arrowroot powder - I should have used more than 1 tsp. I ended up using a gluten free 1 to 1 flour to thicken the sauce instead. It came out great!
Used coconut aminos and arrowroot flour instead of soy and baking soda….and honey instead of brown sugar….my fam is asking me to make a bigger dish again tomorrow!!!
Super easy and very Delicious! Served with rice. Yum!
For Nancy617 and others who think that there is to much Soy Sauce, use the LOW SODIUM soy sauce I don' like a lot of salt either and this is great all the taste and much lower salt
You do not need fresh ginger because it might not be just laying around. I use ground ginger. And I use family size stew meat from Walmart or Costco ( no cutting! )
The sauce was very tasty. I think I may have undercooked the snow peas based on their hardness. The sauce goes great with the beef. I think it would be tastier with other veggies added as well.
Next time I'll Add more ingredients

This was so so good! I wasn't sure I liked snow peas tbh but the dish looked awesome so I had to try. It was gorgeous in the pan (wish I took a pic) made white rice to go with. Only thing was it was super salty. I may try less soy sauce or something next time. But there will be a next time! Can't wait to make it again.
